name: Claap
summary: AI sales intelligence that records calls without putting a bot in the meeting, then turns them into CRM fields, follow-up emails, deal scoring and coaching.
best_for: revenue teams that want every call captured — by default with no notetaker bot in the meeting, though a customisable bot is there for teams that prefer one — and want those calls to end up as CRM fields, coaching and deal signals rather than as transcripts nobody reopens, with enough seats to make a sales conversation worth having
skip_if: you want to buy and test the product yourself, because the tier with the CRM and coaching features is quote-led and even its trial runs through sales; you need a long retention window, since recordings age out after 2 or 3 years below Enterprise; or you need the Claap API, which the comparison table lists on Enterprise only
honest_knock:
The four tiers sell two different products, and only one of them is self-serve. Pro at €24 is the recorder and note-taker. Everything Claap actually markets itself on — CRM auto-complete, AI coaching, deal insights, asking Claap AI a question across all your meetings — starts at Business, €48 per license a month on annual billing, and Business has no self-serve button: it says Book a demo. The pricing FAQ closes the other door too: a trial of Pro or Business is opened by their sales team. So the features you came for cannot be bought or tested without a sales conversation.

Your recordings also expire. Storage runs 3 months on Basic, 2 years on Pro and 3 years on Business; only Enterprise is unlimited. If the call archive is meant to be your evidence trail, that is a deletion date on your own data, and it is in the comparison table rather than in the plan cards.

Two smaller things worth reading twice, and one correction we owe you. The AI credits — 500 per license on Pro, 1,000 on Business, pooled across the workspace — do not meter the summaries: the tooltip is explicit that summaries, chapters and the AI companion use no credits, and a credit is spent on a Claap AI chat, an AI email follow-up, the coaching tab or a generated insight. What is missing is the rate: no price for an extra credit appears anywhere on the page, so a heavy month of coaching and insights cannot be costed before you commit. And the free tier's 300 minutes is a total, not a monthly allowance: it is a sample, not a plan you can sit on.

pricing.notes: (re-read 2026-10-17 on claap.io/pricing, plan cards, FAQ and the full comparison table; first read 2026-09-04) Licenses are priced per license per month, and the page now prints dollars beside euros. Basic is €0: 10 videos per user, 300 minutes of recording in total rather than per month, calendar and conference-call sync, basic AI summary, the Chrome recorder extension, a collaborative workspace and the Claap MCP connector, capped at 5 Basic licenses, no guests, one team, one channel, 3 video uploads and 3 months of recording storage. Pro is €24 or $32 per license a month billed yearly, €30 or $40 monthly: unlimited recordings, 1,000 minutes a month, 500 AI credits per license pooled across the workspace, advanced AI summaries, meeting insights, AI video editing, 10+ integrations, speaker and video insights and private channels, with 50 Basic licenses, 50 guests, 10 uploads a month and 2 years of storage. When we read the tooltips in September, one credit was one Claap AI chat, AI email follow-up, coaching tab or generated insight, and summaries, chapters and the AI companion consumed none. Business is €48 or $60 a month yearly, €60 or $75 monthly: unlimited recording time, 1,000 AI credits per license, ClaapAgent across all meetings, CRM auto-complete, AI-generated emails, AI coaching, deal insights, smart tables, admin recording and sharing controls and priority support, with 50 uploads a month and 3 years of storage. Enterprise is a custom price and adds SSO, SCIM provisioning, the Claap API (marked Not included on every other tier in the comparison table), unlimited Basic licenses, white-glove onboarding and migration support. Basic says Try for free and Pro Start for free; Business and Enterprise say Book a demo, and the FAQ says a trial of Pro or Business is opened by their sales team. Two things from our September reading are gone from the page: the $20-per-seat Power Recorder add-on and the API on every tier.

compare_with.name: Fireflies.ai
compare_with.why: Both record and transcribe meetings and both sit in our database, but they aim at different jobs. Fireflies is the cheaper, broader meeting assistant: it joins the call as a bot, transcribes and summarises, and works for any team that takes notes. Claap is built for revenue teams specifically, records without a bot in the conversation, and puts its money on what happens after the call — CRM fields, deal scoring against MEDDIC or BANT, coaching. Pick Fireflies if you want meetings captured cheaply across the company; pick Claap if your problem is an empty CRM and untrained reps, and you can live with the sales-led purchase.

vendor_mcp.what: Remote server at api.claap.io/mcp over your call recordings, transcripts, synced emails, contacts, companies and deals. It reads, and it also writes back: create fields and views, update deals, add contacts and configure automations.
vendor_mcp.plan: Their FAQ answers it directly: "MCP is on every plan, including the free one." Their AI agents and Zapier, Make and n8n automations sit on Business and Enterprise; their API on Enterprise only.
